decisions.reason: The GK 2.0 high-resolution printer is a flagship hardware platform that was featured on the home page, and the rest of the portfolio depends on it, so its option value is high and the evidence gives no sign of abandonment.
The numbering software module costs little to keep and adds to the core printing systems, so maintaining it is cheap while its value is still building.

The coder for non-absorbent surfaces serves an established niche at low marginal cost, but it never got prominent website coverage, so it carries somewhat more risk of being consolidated into newer models.

The CodeScan app already succeeded the PharmaScan app, which shows the firm does replace products, but upkeep is cheap and the app supports the verification ecosystem, so the option is worth keeping open.
Inline code verification fits the growing demand for track-and-trace, and its prospects are still unfolding, so keeping it at modest cost preserves its upside.
The layout design software was promoted on the home page and is central to running the printers, so it is a low-cost, high-value option to keep.
